extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of classical philosophy (readers of Plato's Republic)
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive norms and evaluative criteria for founding and judging a just city and its citizens (especially guardians) as set out in Plato's Republic Book IV: rules about class roles, education, property, music, military training, and the four cardinal virtues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on guardians handling precious metals
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians may not touch or handle silver or gold, or be under the same roof with them, or wear them, or drink from them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: precious metals are a source of corruption; forbidding contact prevents guardians becoming corrupt. Presented as a strict rule to preserve the guardians' purity and the State's salvation; violation leads to them becoming housekeepers/husbandmen and eventual tyranny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians must not acquire private property or money
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians should not acquire homes, lands, or moneys of their own, because possession of these turns guardians into housekeepers and husbandmen instead of true guardians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanation: Private wealth creates attachments, envy, faction and internal terror; it degrades guardians' character and threatens the state's stability. This is framed as necessary to keep guardians 'true saviours' rather than destroyers of the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians are fed but not paid with money
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians are maintained (fed) by the State but are not paid in money or allowed to possess wealth for leisure or luxuries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: to prevent mercenary motives and ensure guardians do their duty rather than pursue personal pleasures (mistresses, travel etc.). This arrangement supports the argument that they may be the happiest of men despite lacking private wealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education and nurture are the primary instrument of legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: The core of good legislation is the education and nurture of citizens: if citizens are well educated they will follow the laws and social regulations without detailed enactments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: legislators should focus on formative education (music and gymnastics, upbringing) rather than exhaustive legal minutiae; a properly educated populace will organically follow required customs and rules. Education is presented as the 'one sufficient' thing for founding the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve traditional music and gymnastic; forbid musical innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Music and gymnastic must be preserved in their original form and no innovation in modes of music should be permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasoning: Musical innovations are dangerous because changes in musical modes lead to changes in the fundamental laws and character of the State. Anti-pattern: praising 'new songs' or new kinds of song is to be feared and prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early, strict training of youth to prevent lawlessness
rubrics_metrics.description: Youth should be trained from the first in a stricter system; amusement that becomes lawless leads to lawless manners and customs which corrupt the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation: begin with disciplined play and music to instill order; orderly habits developed in youth become lifelong and help raise fallen places in the State. Anti-pattern: laissez-faire amusement that fosters licence and invades contracts and laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: One person — one function (specialization of roles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual should perform the one work for which nature has fitted him; one man should practise one thing only and not be a busybody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justice is defined politically as each class and person doing their own business. Mixing roles (trader becoming warrior, warrior becoming legislator) is ruinous to the State. Policy implication: enforce clear class boundaries and occupational specialization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians must be a small, distinct ruling class possessing knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: The guardians (rulers) should be the smallest class and the possessors of the knowledge which counsels for the good of the whole State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanation: Wisdom that guides whole-state policy resides in the guardians; their small number is natural and desirable. They provide the 'good counsel' that makes the State truly wise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit the size of the State consistent with unity
rubrics_metrics.description: The State should be allowed to increase only so far as is consistent with unity; it should be accounted one and self-sufficing rather than very large or many States combined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: expansion that compromises unity is to be avoided. A moderate-sized, self-sufficient polity is preferable to a superficially larger but internally divided conglomerate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective social mobility among guardians' offspring
rubrics_metrics.description: Offspring of guardians who are inferior should be degraded; offspring of lower classes who are naturally superior should be elevated into the guardianship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanism: promote or demote children based on natural aptitude so each individual is placed in the role nature intended. This maintains class-function fit without rigid hereditary privilege.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against degeneration caused by both wealth and poverty
rubrics_metrics.description: Both wealth (leading to luxury and indolence) and poverty (preventing proper tools/training) cause workmen and arts to degenerate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication: maintain conditions that avoid extreme wealth or extreme poverty among classes whose crafts and duties are essential for the State's wellbeing; guardians must watch for these evils to prevent social decay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military excellence via comprehensive training (music + gymnastics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Warriors/athletes should be trained in music and gymnastics so they become expert fighters capable of overcoming numerous but less-skilled adversaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogy: a perfect boxer can overcome multiple well-to-do but unskilled opponents if trained and tactically adept. Training fixes the 'dye' of lawful opinion about dangers (see courage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundational role of music in forming the guardians' fortress
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians must 'lay the foundations of their fortress in music' because lawlessness easily steals in through amusement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Music shapes soul and customs; careful musical education is essential to prevent the gradual slide from harmless amusement to lawless customs and ultimately to the overthrow of rights. Damon invoked as authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courage defined as preserved true opinion about dangers
rubrics_metrics.description: Courage is the preservation, under all circumstances (pleasure, pain, desire, fear), of the opinion implanted by law about what is to be feared and what is not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustration: dyeing analogy — proper early education fixes opinions indelibly as a dye on prepared cloth. Distinguish 'citizen courage' (law-formed) from mere animal or slave courage (uninstructed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperance as harmony and self-mastery across classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Temperance (self-mastery) is the ordering and controlling of pleasures and desires, a harmony of the naturally superior and inferior about who should rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a state-wide virtue, temperance extends through all classes and is present when rulers and subjects agree on the rightful rulers. It differs from wisdom and courage which reside in particular parts/classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wisdom as knowledge of the whole residing in rulers
rubrics_metrics.description: Wisdom in the State is the knowledge found in the guardians who counsel about the whole State, not knowledge of particular crafts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish craft-knowledge (carpenter, farmer) from the rulers' knowledge that advises for the good of the whole. This knowledge is the basis for calling the State 'good in counsel' and 'truly wise.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Justice as each class doing its own work, not meddling
rubrics_metrics.description: Justice in the State is when trader, auxiliary (soldier), and guardian each do their own business; injustice is meddling, interchange of functions or one person doing many roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational test: when occupations, implements, and duties are kept distinct and individuals perform their natural role, the city is just. Conversely, the greatest evil is the change or mingling of class functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave sacred rites and the ordering of religious matters to the divine interpreter
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions of temples, sacrifices, rites for the dead, and the service of gods and heroes are matters for Apollo (the ancestral deity) rather than human legislators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislators should be humble about religious mysteries; these chiefest matters are beyond the founders' expertise and ought to be entrusted to the divine interpreter or religious tradition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive legislation about trivial social particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not wise to legislate minutiae of deportment (standing for elders, dress, hair, domestic manners) because such enactments are unlikely to be lasting; education should instill these norms instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance: rely on upbringing and custom for small social rules; legislating every detail is unnecessary in a well-ordered State and typical of ill-ordered polities.
